analysis.title: Takes from 20+ Power/Cooling Companies - Open Compute Project Conf. & Deep Dive
key_insights: Mizuho reviewed the 2026 OCP Global Summit sessions from 20+ power and cooling suppliers and chip, cloud and test companies. It sees a gradual transition to 800VDC, with AC infrastructure remaining integral across multiple deployment configurations.
Takeaway 1: the move toward MW-scale racks makes 800VDC distribution imperative.
Takeaway 2: NVIDIA's GPU/rack rollout sets the pace of 800V adoption. Sidecars and AC/DC coexistence support investment ahead of native-800V racks, and Kyber's rollout is the key watch item.

Takeaway 3: liquid cooling remains among the most attractive structural growth opportunities for equipment providers. Rising penetration and broader compute/power applications drive growth ahead of underlying data center capacity expansion.
Takeaway 4: power constraints are sharpening suppliers' focus on cutting consumption and conversion losses so more scarce power goes to compute.
Takeaway 5: modular designs are becoming critical to scaling data center build-outs because systems can be manufactured and tested off-site, then installed and commissioned faster.

Eaton: moving AC/DC conversion outside the compute rack changes the distribution and protection equipment needed. Eaton illustrated 125A circuits carrying about 100kW each at 800V. Mizuho sees ETN's opportunity spanning conversion, DC distribution panels, busway, protection and system integration.

Eaton: DC current does not fall to zero periodically like AC, so fault interruption is harder, and batteries and capacitors can keep feeding a fault. Eaton named four functions needed: fault detection, rapid interruption, physical isolation and backup protection. That supports demand for solid-state or hybrid breakers alongside disconnects, fuses and interlocks.
A joint ABB/Eaton session stressed common voltage ranges, grounding practices, connectors and controls so equipment from different suppliers works together.

Johnson Controls: in its 500MW facility example, cooling demand falls from 175MW to 75MW. That frees 100MW for IT and lifts compute capacity from 325MW to 425MW (31%) without raising total facility power. JCI describes these figures as illustrative.

Johnson Controls: a chip-to-chiller simulation of about 2MW of IT load with AI agents controlling chilled-water temperature and CDU pump speed improved tokens per unit of energy by 11.5% and cut partial PUE by 10.3%. Caveats: a fixed 15C chilled-water baseline was used, and in the two-agent setup only two of eight models stayed below the 85C throttling threshold.

Vertiv: customers should design facilities for several generations of AI racks, and AC and DC architectures will coexist for years. Busway and cooling pipes are hard to replace, so they should be sized for future loads while tap-off boxes, breakers and rack connections stay flexible. Vertiv proposed AC/DC-rated busway, with product development and compliance work still pending.

Vertiv: the solid-state breaker (local fast fault interruption) is distinct from the DC Fault Manager (system-wide protection and restart). Vertiv also outlined a possible shift of UPS functionality upstream to medium-voltage systems tied to longer-duration battery storage.

Vertiv and AMD cooling workstream: a large CDU alone does not ensure enough cooling reaches the racks, since pipe sizing, pressure loss, coolant cleanliness and flushing set usable capacity. Improved procedures cut pre-commissioning from seven weeks to one.

NVIDIA's timeline has an intermediate stage where racks receive 800V but keep 54V internally, followed by native 800V inside the rack. Mizuho's working assumptions are Rubin Ultra in the Oberon NVL72 rack in 2027 and the larger Kyber NVL144 rack around Feynman in 2028+.
NVIDIA's targeted equipment readiness dates are sidecars in 3Q26, PowerCenters in 2Q27 and PowerBlocks in 1Q28. Customer adoption and GPU/rack launches could follow separate timelines.

Mizuho: a longer transition does not automatically mean more sidecar demand, because customers whose racks stay within existing power-system limits could defer upgrades. External conversion, DC busway, connectors and protection can develop ahead of native 800V racks, while upstream AC switchgear and transformers stay integral to Options A and B.

NVIDIA's three deployment options: A is sidecar power racks added to existing AC distribution, B is shared Power Centers with DC busway, and C is facility-level Power Blocks for new builds. The Option C illustration uses six active 5MW blocks plus one reserve, for 30MW active and 35MW installed capacity.

nVent (not covered): in AMD's Helios example, a 246kW rack captures 89% of heat in liquid and leaves about 27kW in exhaust air. nVent's rear-door heat exchanger moves that heat into water. More liquid cooling adds rack-level cooling content and reduces the load on room-level CRAH units.

Delta (not covered): about 30kW of conversion losses per MW at 97% power-supply efficiency. It showed a 660kW power rack with 480kW of battery backup, 90/108kW 800V-to-54V shelves, a 5,000A liquid-cooled busbar and an 800V-powered 2.5MW CDU with a 4C approach temperature.

Megmeet (not covered): a fully liquid-cooled 110kW AC/DC shelf delivering 54V in two rack units, and a 95kW one-unit 800V-to-54V shelf. It cited potential facility-capex savings of up to about 10% for an optimized fully liquid-cooled greenfield design, dependent on facility assumptions.

Oracle: about 90% of its observed physical-link failures come from contamination. It discussed 3M's Expanded Beam Optical technology and is co-chairing an effort to build an interoperable supplier ecosystem around it. Mizuho reads this as customer validation for MMM.

Daikin: modeled a 1MW IT load across 18 U.S. grid regions and found dry cooling favored on utility cost in markets including ERCOT and PJM East. The result depends on local electricity and water prices.

Alfa Laval, Gamma Technologies and STULZ study at 2.3MW cooling duty: facility water flow ranged from about 660 to 940 gpm, annual cooling energy varied about 17% under Dallas weather, and heat-exchanger hardware cost varied about threefold. The results were modeled.

CoolIT: at an illustrative 70% liquid/30% air split, a 250kW rack leaves 75kW and a 500kW rack leaves 150kW for air cooling. The roadmap extends cold plates to memory, optics, storage and power components. A cold plate was validated at 15kW with 45C facility water.

Microsoft/Lenovo: widening racks from 600mm to 900mm gives about 50% more airflow area and early data show 20-30% lower server fan power per kW cooled for CPUs of 650W to 1,000W+. Rack-level validation is pending. This supports a continued role for air-handling equipment.

Gates (not covered): hose formulation affects cooling reliability, with differing residue levels across peroxide-cured EPDM samples after eight weeks at 80C. It ran a two-inch hose at about 9.4 m/s with no eroded particles detected so far, and testing is ongoing.
Auras (not covered) presented a smart CDU with predictive flow adjustment and microchannel cold plates for 45C coolant inlet. These are design capabilities, not quantified savings.
Keysight (not covered) advocated system-level validation of AI infrastructure with its KAI Data Center Builder, Conformance Builder and Inference Builder tools.
Mizuho Exhibit 14 maps 800VDC roadmaps and sees sidecars as a key opportunity ahead of native DC adoption. Exhibit 15 shows Mizuho expects a more gradual transition to native 800VDC.
The report includes the Mizuho price target framework for 29 stocks. It initiates SpaceX (SPCX) at Outperform with a $200 PT and upgrades IDEX (IEX), with PTs listed per company.

Oracle framed AI network design around reliability and power efficiency at OCP.

sector_views.sector: Data center power and cooling equipment
sector_views.rationale: Liquid cooling is among the most attractive structural growth opportunities, and external 800V conversion, DC distribution and protection spending can develop ahead of native 800V racks.
Mizuho lays out base, bull and bear cases for 29 names. Valuations vary widely and several large names are held at Neutral on valuation.

risk_factors: Kyber timing: a longer transition to native 800V racks could defer sidecar demand for customers whose racks stay within existing power-system limits.
JCI's simulated efficiency gains did not consistently keep GPU temperatures acceptable, and real building automation integration and larger-scale validation remain ahead.
Vertiv's AC/DC-rated busway still needs product development and compliance work.
Hyperscale data center spending retrenchment is a risk for VRT, ETN and SPCX, including a technical crack in AI multiples.
SPCX: Starship delays, xAI execution requiring about 225% revenue CAGR, Musk's 82.4% voting control, and lock-up releases in December 2026 and June 2027.
MMM: PFAS liabilities and weak consumer-related end markets.
Residential HVAC and consumer weakness affect CARR, WSO, LII and WHR.
Many 800V products are design capabilities or modeled results and not yet quantified operating savings.

tension_points.bull_case: MW-scale racks make 800VDC distribution imperative, and external conversion, DC busway and protection content can develop ahead of native 800V racks through sidecars and Power Centers.
tension_points.bear_case: A longer transition to Kyber does not automatically mean more sidecar demand, because customers whose racks stay within existing power-system limits could defer upgrades.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Kyber's rollout timing, which Mizuho assumes around Feynman in 2028+, is the key milestone for native-rack equipment content.

tension_points.bull_case: Liquid cooling penetration is rising, and CoolIT argues for capturing nearly all server heat in liquid, which adds rack-level cooling content.
tension_points.bear_case: Microsoft and Lenovo showed that 900mm racks can extend air cooling's economic life for general-purpose CPU workloads with 20-30% lower fan power per kW cooled.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Liquid remains appropriate when component heat loads, heat concentration or site constraints exceed what the wider air-cooled design can handle.

theme_stances.key_argument: External conversion, DC busway, connectors and protection demand can develop ahead of native 800V racks while AC switchgear and transformers stay integral.
theme_stances.evidence: Kyber's rollout remains the key watch item

theme_stances.key_argument: Liquid cooling is among the most attractive structural growth opportunities for equipment providers, growing ahead of underlying data center capacity expansion.
theme_stances.evidence: liquid cooling remains among the most attractive structural growth opportunities

theme_stances.key_argument: Cutting cooling and conversion losses frees scarce power for compute, which supports the investment case for efficiency-focused suppliers.
